articles.title: Chinese 'spy' Alice Huang's companies invested in DeepSeek, promised Nvidia's Blackwell chips
articles.summary: Companies linked to alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang have invested in Chinese artificial intelligence firm DeepSeek and committed to supplying Nvidia's
articles.body: Companies linked to alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang have invested in Chinese artificial intelligence firm DeepSeek and committed to supplying Nvidia's Blackwell chips, according to a report by The Information.Blackwell is Nvidia's latest generation of graphics processing units (GPUs) and AI accelerators. Built on the company's Blackwell GPU microarchitecture, it succeeds the older Hopper architecture and is designed to power large-scale artificial intelligence, heavy-duty data centres and high-performance computing.Alice, also known as Alice Wang or Huang Le, is a Chinese businesswoman whose links with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed have come under scrutiny.Meanwhile, Singapore authorities have issued Alice a stern warning and barred her from re-entering the country after finding that she provided inaccurate information during investigations into Megaspeed.Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said the Singapore Police Force (SPF) assessed that Alice had attempted to mislead investigators to downplay her role in the company.The probe centres on suspected false declarations involving the purchase of servers and other related offences. The SPF and Singapore Customs launched separate investigations into Megaspeed and others in February 2025.Alice's association with the Nvidia CEO reportedly dates back several years. According to reports, she was introduced to Jensen through her husband, corporate investor Kang Weigh, around a decade before reports of her alleged relationship with the billionaire executive emerged.Kang had business dealings with Jensen in the 2010s while acquiring Chinese video game companies, a source familiar with the couple told The Information.Chinese media reports suggest that Kang and Alice used their association with Jensen to secure business opportunities over the years. Some social media posts claimed that Kang would flaunt his wife's relationship with the Nvidia CEO to clients. Alice also regularly shared photographs with Jensen on her WeChat account.Her proximity to Jensen was allegedly a major factor in her business dealings in China.Their more recent business dealings reportedly took place through Megaspeed, which conducted billions of dollars in business with Nvidia. The Singapore-based data centre company remains under investigation over suspected false declarations linked to server purchases.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: 'Legend replaces a legend': Trump wants Tim Cook to replace Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has brought Apple's Tim Cook into the conversation around Nvidia's leadership, suggesting that the Apple CEO should replace
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has brought Apple's Tim Cook into the conversation around Nvidia's leadership, suggesting that the Apple CEO should replace Jensen Huang at the chipmaker.In a post on Truth Social, Trump called Cook the only person fit to take over from Huang, who has resigned with immediate effect.“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend! President DONALD J. TRUMP “Trump's suggestion comes after Cook stepped down as Apple’s chief back in September after leading the Cupertino-based company for more than a decade. Trump also recalled his association with Cook, describing him as “an incredible guy” and saying their professional relationship began during his first term as president, when Cook approached him for help with an issue.Nvidia's sudden leadership changeNvidia's board announced on Thursday that Jensen Huang had stepped down as the chipmaker's president, CEO and board member, with the resignation taking immediate effect.The announcement followed reports of two alleged affairs involving Huang. One involves a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing. Another report alleged that Huang had an extramarital relationship with a senior company executive who reported directly to him.A person familiar with the matter said Nvidia's board had met on Wednesday to consider Huang's removal.The company acknowledged the contributions of its outgoing chief, saying, “Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. Shares of Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, crashed in opening trade on Thursday as its CEO Jensen Huang resigned.“NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” it added.The board has named chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent successor. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and owns around 3.61% of the company, is its fourth-largest investor. He will also give up his board position.Huang's departure was followed by a steep fall in Nvidia shares during Thursday's opening trade. The stock dropped 13.09% to $150.98, taking the company's market capitalisation below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025.The exit marks a major leadership change for the AI industry, particularly for Nvidia, which Huang transformed into a dominant force in artificial intelligence.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Norwest to hike investments in Indian manufacturing, healthcare and tech after $4bn global fund raise
articles.summary: MUMBAI: US-based Norwest has raised a record $4 billion fund, its largest in 65 years, part of which will be used to expand investments in India,
articles.body: MUMBAI: US-based Norwest has raised a record $4 billion fund, its largest in 65 years, part of which will be used to expand investments in India, particularly in manufacturing, industrial services and healthcare. It currently deploys $250-350 million annually in the country.Norwest 18 takes the firm's capital under management to $18 billion and will fund venture and growth equity investments across technology, healthcare and consumer sectors in the US, India and Israel.The firm has maintained steady investments across market cycles for two decades, said Niren Shah, managing director and head of Norwest India. "Norwest is currently deploying around $250-350 million annually in India, which is higher than the earlier levels of investment. Norwest remains very bullish on India's long-term prospects," he said.While fintech and consumer remain core sectors, Norwest is increasing its focus on industrials and healthcare. It will pursue growth equity, venture, platform and buyout investments. "Industrials and Healthcare are becoming increasingly prominent in our investment strategy. Norwest will continue to remain a Multi-strategy fund and focus both on Growth Equity and Venture investments, while also looking to undertake more Platform and Buyout transactions," Shah said.The firm sees opportunities in value-added and precision manufacturing and industrial services, driven by Make in India and global manufacturers' growing emphasis on quality and supply-chain diversification over cost alone. "Our investment approach will continue to be centred on Growth Equity, with a greater focus on Precision Manufacturing and Industrial services," Shah said. Healthcare and fintech will remain priorities, alongside venture investments in AI and deep tech.Since launching Norwest 17 in April 2024, the firm has made over 87 investments and helped more than 30 portfolio companies achieve exits through IPOs and acquisitions. These include Indian listings Swiggy and Amagi Media Labs, US listings BillionToOne, MBX Biosciences and Omada Health, and acquisitions of Qualified by Salesforce, Veza by ServiceNow and Ouro Medicines by Gilead Sciences.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Decline in oil prices could save India up to $9bn in FY27
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Moderation in international crude oil prices could save India up to $9 billion on its oil import bill in the current fiscal and help temper
articles.body: MUMBAI: Moderation in international crude oil prices could save India up to $9 billion on its oil import bill in the current fiscal and help temper wholesale price inflation, even as the impact on retail inflation is likely to remain limited, according to a Bank of Baroda research report.The report, authored by economist Dipanwita Mazumdar, estimates that a 10% decline in international oil prices from current levels could reduce India's oil import bill by $9-10 billion, equivalent to around 0.2% of nominal GDP. This would also support the current account deficit (CAD).International oil prices fell 22.2% between Oct 30 and Nov 10, following expectations of a possible peace agreement between the US and Iran after the US midterm elections. However, escalating attacks involving Saudi-led forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen could affect the sustainability of the decline. Brent crude futures were trading around $81 per barrel.The moderation in oil prices is expected to have a greater impact on wholesale price inflation (WPI) than consumer price inflation (CPI). Oil-sensitive components account for around 8.8% of the WPI basket. A 10% decline in crude prices could lower WPI inflation by 13-14 basis points through direct and indirect effects on petroleum products, aviation turbine fuel (ATF) and manufactured goods.The impact on CPI is expected to be largely neutral because retail prices of petrol, diesel and LPG are administered. Restaurant prices are also unlikely to respond to a temporary decline in oil prices, while the pass-through to airfares will depend on airlines and demand conditions.The report noted that consumers were largely insulated when international crude prices rose sharply, as retail fuel prices remained unchanged. A decline in global prices is therefore unlikely to translate into lower retail selling prices. However, the correction could narrow the divergence between CPI and WPI, offering some relief to manufacturers whose input costs had risen without a corresponding increase in consumer prices.On the fiscal front, higher fertiliser subsidies could increase the fiscal deficit by 0.2-0.3% of GDP. The FY27 Budget had allocated Rs 1.7 lakh crore for urea and fertiliser subsidies, including Rs 1.2 lakh crore for urea and Rs 54,000 crore under the nutrient-based subsidy (NBS) scheme.The NBS allocation has since increased to Rs 1.03 lakh crore, including Rs 41,534 crore for the kharif season and Rs 62,370 crore for the rabi season. Lower profitability of oil marketing companies could also weigh on non-tax revenue. However, higher nominal GDP growth and disinvestment receipts could provide some support to the fiscal position.Lower oil prices could also support the rupee, alongside a revival in foreign portfolio investor (FPI) inflows. Net FPI inflows rose to $7.1 billion in Nov, compared with outflows of $2.5 billion in Oct. The report attributed the revival partly to greater investor interest in emerging markets amid policy uncertainty in the US and moderation in AI-led valuations.Bank of Baroda expects the rupee to trade in the range of Rs 93-95 against the dollar in the near term, compared with its earlier forecast of Rs 94-95. However, the dollar index and expectations of tighter monetary policy in major economies remain key factors to watch.The impact of lower oil prices on bond yields is expected to be limited. While cheaper crude could provide temporary relief to India's 10-year government bond yield, global yields and domestic monetary policy are likely to keep borrowing costs elevated. The report expects another 50 basis points of rate hikes in FY27, which could limit the decline in yields.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Will Social Security go broke in 2032? What retirees need to know.
articles.summary: The looming shortfall in Social Security benefits is projected to result in a 22% to 26% cut by 2032. What to know about whether Social Security benefits wil...
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

The looming shortfall in Social Security benefits is projected to result in a 22% to 26% cut by 2032, according to the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) and the latest 2026 Social Security Trustees' report.

While fewer workers funding more recipients is widely blamed for the financial pressures facing Social Security, a new study says "shifting income patterns" have also weakened the program's solvency — and offers a solution.

Rising wages among high-income earners often exceed Social Security's taxable cap, Richard W. Johnson of the AARP Public Policy Institute noted in a new analysis. Meanwhile, corporate earnings and investment returns are flourishing.

By lifting the payroll tax cap and taxing some of the investment income of high earners, Social Security could pay full benefits until 2059, 25 years longer than current projections.

"These changes would help close Social Security's financing gap without requiring lower- or moderate-income people to contribute more," Johnson wrote.

Here is what's happening and what needs to be done to save the system every American worker has helped fund.

In short: Fewer workers are funding more recipients.

In 1960, there were 5.1 workers paying into the system for every Social Security recipient. That ratio fell throughout the 1980s and 1990s, and when the oldest baby boomers turned 62 in 2008, a dramatic decline began.

In 2024, there were 2.7 workers per beneficiary.

With longer lifetimes and fewer workers per Social Security recipient, the financial drain on the system is dramatic.

As the AARP report observed, national income distribution over the past 40 years has also contributed to Social Security's dwindling revenue.

"Although payroll taxes paid primarily by middle-income workers currently account for 91% of Social Security revenue, the relative economic position of these workers has steadily declined."

A recent UCLA/Cornell study confirmed the widely held belief that most people think Social Security is going broke and expect "benefits to cease completely" when it does.

What most people don't consider, the research concluded, are the funds continuing to flow into the system.

Even if reserve funds are depleted, American workers will continue to pay into Social Security through payroll taxes deducted from their paychecks each payday. That means Social Security benefits will continue to be paid, but are likely to be reduced.

"Benefits will continue to be payable after reserve depletion, but not in full unless legislative action is taken," the American Academy of Actuaries noted in an analysis of the SSA's trustees report.

As Social Security collects payroll taxes, it pays out benefits to retired workers and eligible family members, as well as death and disability benefits. Workers pay 6.2% from their wages, and employers match that amount. Self-employed individuals pay the full 12.4% of Social Security taxes. Both are capped at a maximum wage.

Medicare taxes and benefits are also collected.

If Social Security collects more than is paid out in benefits, the excess is placed in trust fund reserves and invested in Treasurys to pay future benefits.

"When people talk of Social Security 'going bankrupt,' they are (incorrectly or misleadingly) referring to a scenario where the Social Security Trust Fund has no reserves (it has become 'depleted') and tax revenue is insufficient to cover existing benefits obligations," the Roosevelt Institute, a nonprofit think tank, explained in an analysis.

The fact is, Social Security can pay full benefits for a few more years but then faces a "significant, though manageable, funding shortfall," the institute added.

If action isn't taken, yes, benefits could be cut.

"If reforms are not enacted soon, recipients could see a large decrease in their benefits," the Peter G. Peterson Foundation, a nonprofit think tank, said in an analysis. "If lawmakers act soon to address the trust fund shortfalls, they will be able to phase in changes gradually and responsibly in a way that does not harm vulnerable populations. However, delaying reform would require larger changes to the program."

"Restoring balance to the Social Security system could involve raising taxes, changing benefits, or a combination of these two approaches," the American Academy of Actuaries reported.

The Academy lists possible ways of increasing revenue into the system:

Increasing taxes paid by high-wage earners

Gradually raising the full retirement age

Lowering the inflation index used to adjust benefits

Under current assumptions, the actuarial organization estimates that it would take an immediate 3.65% increase in the combined employee/employer tax rate (to a total 16.05% of taxable payroll), or an immediate 22.4% cut in benefits to current and future recipients.

Either would "balance the system over the next 75 years," the organization concluded.

The American Academy of Actuaries has a web app that demystifies Social Security through animation and voiceovers. The Social Security Challenge explains how the system works, the looming funding shortfall, and possible financial solutions.

As explained by David Mendes, director of communications for the Academy, the web resource "immerses users in an animated virtual trek where they learn about the program, the financing shortfall that could (if unaddressed by Congress) lead to future cuts in scheduled benefits, and how different reform options they select along their journey could help address the shortfall."

Graphically illustrating the problem and possible solutions may be the only way to truly understand the challenges Social Security faces.

articles.title: Happiest Health gets Rs 500 cr tech boost from Soota
articles.summary: Ashok Soota to invest Rs 500 crore in Happiest Health tech over 5 years, boosting digital health apps like DiaBeater and ColonE after Happiest Minds stake sale.
articles.body: Bengaluru: At 83, Ashok Soota remains upbeat about his healthcare venture, backing it with fresh funds to accelerate growth. He has earmarked Rs 500 crore from the proceeds of the sale of his stake in Happiest Minds to ITC Infotech to accelerate technology investments at Happiest Health over the next five years. About half of this amount will go towards its digital health business, Happiest Digital Health, the company’s fifth business unit, which will begin with a portfolio of 11 digital applications to be rolled out over the next 18 months.Soota said a substantial part of the Rs 1,330 crore proceeds from the sale of his 22.1% stake in Happiest Minds to ITC Infotech would be channelled into healthcare initiatives, including Happiest Health and a non-profit entity, SKAN Research Trust. He had previously committed Rs 200 crore towards SKAN, focused on ageing and neurological research.“Investment will come from the proceeds of the ITC Infotech transaction. Even after the merger, I will remain the single largest individual shareholder in the merged entity. My technology connection will continue. It’s a very important part of the business.”Digital health is a fast-growing segment of healthcare, expected to reach $1.8 trillion globally by 2033, growing at 25% annually, he said. The move is also aimed at overcoming the geographical limitations of physical healthcare providers.“Even companies that have been around for 30 years are present in only two, three or four cities. Some of the largest players derive 44% of their business from one city and another 40% from a second city, with only a small presence elsewhere. So nobody can reach out too far,” Soota said.He said the digital health business would draw on the medical expertise developed within Happiest Health, with doctors guiding the design and clinical content of individual applications. Happiest Minds is developing the technology, including small language models (SLMs), while medical inputs will come from specialists.The company is placing particular emphasis on diabetes management through DiaBeater, a doctor-led, AI-assisted application that uses glucose-monitoring technology. India has more than 100 million people living with diabetes, making continuous care a significant opportunity, Soota said. Dr Kashinath, who heads the endocrinology practice at Happiest Health and has 28 years of experience, including at the UK’s NHS, is guiding the medical framework for the application.Other planned offerings include Pediatric Expert and Cardio Edge. The company is also launching ColonE, a gut microbiome test that uses next-generation sequencing to analyse microbial DNA from a stool sample. The process generates about 5GB of data, which is used to prepare a report that nutritionists draw on to guide dietary and lifestyle changes. ColonE is a wellness offering, not a diagnostic test.SKAN Research Trust has conducted more than 1,000 gut microbiome tests and built a substantial data repository, Soota said. He identified gut microbiome research and bioinformatics as two important areas of work at SKAN, adding that it would remain a non-commercial entity, although monetisation avenues could be explored later.Happiest Health has identified 15-20 additional specialities for potential digital applications, though not all may lend themselves to digital delivery. The company will assess the market size and consumers’ willingness to pay in each segment before firming up revenue projections.Soota said the company expects to prepare internal financial plans by March and may share tentative business projections by June. It also plans to present its broader healthcare services business once six or seven facilities are ready, potentially by mid-2027.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Ola Electric loss narrows 13%, revenue falls 41%
articles.summary: Ola Electric’s Q2 net loss narrowed 13% to Rs 362 crore as expenses fell, but total income dropped 41% to Rs 448 crore amid a shift to dealers.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Ola Electric’s net loss narrowed 13.4% year-on-year to Rs 362 crore in the September quarter, helped by lower expenses, as the electric two-wheeler maker shifts to dealers and winds down its company-run stores.Total income fell 40.7% to Rs 448 crore from Rs 756 crore a year earlier. Compared with the June quarter, the loss widened from Rs 336 crore, while total income declined from Rs 484 crore.Total expenses fell to Rs 639 crore from Rs 893 crore a year earlier. Finance costs declined to Rs 63 crore from Rs 109 crore. A revision in the estimated useful lives of certain assets reduced depreciation expenses by Rs 38 crore during the quarter.Ola said it stopped accepting orders through its direct-to-consumer stores on Nov 1 and that the network would largely close by Dec. It had appointed 255 dealer partners operating 319 stores as of Nov 8, and plans to reach about 450 stores by Dec and 700 by March 2027.The company expects the store closures to reduce operating expenses by about Rs 50 crore. Dealers pay for vehicles when ordering and hold inventory themselves, improving Ola’s working capital cycle, it said.“Demand is ahead of supply, and we can sell every vehicle we produce,” Ola said in its shareholder letter. It attributed its production constraints to suppliers ramping up, rather than its own manufacturing capacity. About 5,000 paid orders due for delivery in September were pushed into October because chargers were unavailable. It expects production to reach about 25,000 vehicles in Dec.Auditor B S R & Co said Ola had treated Rs 57 crore in penalties as waived before govt approved it. It said Ola should have recorded another Rs 11 crore in penalties in the June quarter and shown the full waiver in the September quarter. Ola said it expected to meet the conditions attached to the waiver.Operating cash outflow widened to Rs 403 crore in the first half from Rs 343 crore a year earlier. After the quarter ended, Ola received about Rs 600 crore in application money towards its Rs 1,000 crore rights issue.The company also said it had commissioned 6 GWh of battery-cell capacity and expected incentives under govt’s production-linked incentive scheme to start coming in from the next quarter.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Huang high, Huang low: Nvidia's boss quits as second affair comes to light
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: For 33 years, Jensen Huang held all the chips. He proved less adept at keeping his private life under wraps.
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: For 33 years, Jensen Huang held all the chips. He proved less adept at keeping his private life under wraps. On Thursday, the man who powered the AI revolution resigned as CEO of Nvidia, the company he founded and catapulted to a global #1, after a second extra-marital affair, this one with a company associate, surfaced in the media even as the first one with an alleged Chinese spy was roiling the tech and geo-political world.“Nvidia board of directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, CEO, and a member of the Board, effective immediately,” the company said in a statement, adding that Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Nvidia, has agreed to serve as Interim CEO until a permanent successor has been named. It said the Board is initiating a search for a permanent CEO and will consider internal and external candidates.“Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” the statement said. Nvidia’s ten-member board includes Indian-American Aarti Shah, formerly of Eli Lilly.Indeed, Huang, Nvidia’s only CEO since its founding in 1993, was synonymous with the company that he built into the world's most valuable semiconductor business, in the process becoming the indispensable impresario of the AI revolution. But apparently, bossing over AI and chips was easier than processing moral clarity when it came to relationships.On Wednesday evening, even as the tech and political world was still grappling with the purported Chinese honeytrap that the Nvidia honcho fell into, the New York Times reported a second extramarital affair allegedly with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice-president of healthcare, who reported directly to Huang. There was no coming back from this one.The company board initially appeared to stand by him following glowing testimonials from President Trump, who repeatedly vouched for his character despite reports of his being entrapped by a Chinese spy.The Nvidia board's November 8 statement had struck a reassuring note, expressing confidence in Huang and asserting there was no reason to believe that Nvidia's national security or corporate secrets had been compromised, while announcing an independent investigation into the matter. Four days later, the confidence evaporated after the second alleged affair, which company insiders were apparently aware of, leaked it to the NYT.Beyond the turmoil in Nvidia, where Huang’s two adult children Madison and Spencer have director-level roles, there is now considerable embarrassment for President Trump, who invested political capital vouching for Huang’s character. He called him an “honorable man” and a “great guy who… has done an amazing job for our country.” Hours after Huang quit, Trump did not address the scandal but said in a post on Truth Social, “NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!”But the fallout from the scandal goes beyond the Nvidia boardroom and the tech world. It is already shaking up Washington’s political establishment, drawing in Trump’s cabinet secretaries some of whom were at odds with each other as intelligence reports emerged over the past year of Huang’s affair with the alleged Chinese spy. Democrats are also champing at the bit to begin investigations and hearings into the matter.According to several accounts, it was secretary of state Marco Rubio, who is also the US national security advisor, who supervised a classified intelligence memorandum warning the administration about Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Rubio is also reported to have personally briefed Trump aboard Air Force One in May, before Huang joined the presidential delegation in Alaska for the onward flight to China.Trump not only allowed his favoured technology executive to travel with him to China but continued to give him character certificates, and his subsequent claim that he had not known about the intelligence concerns has now become an uncomfortable subject of scrutiny.The controversy has also drawn in two other cabinet secretaries: commerce secretary Howard Lutnick and treasury secretary Scott Bessent. According to a report in Axios, Bessent raised the question of the administration's failure to place Megaspeed, alleged to be a front company Alice Huang worked for, on the Commerce Department's Entity List, which would restrict its access to American technology. Lutnick, who like Huang has argued that excessive restrictions risk sacrificing commercial opportunities and provoking a trade war, reportedly muttered that he needed to check with Trump.Trump himself has been careful about ratcheting up temperature on the affair given an upcoming meeting next week with China’s President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, and Nvidia’s criticality to not just American tech primacy but also to the US stock market, a Trump obsession which he seems to believe is an indicator of economic health.Nvidia is not simply a chip manufacturer; its graphics processors are the picks and shovels of the AI gold rush, powering the data centers and frontier models being built by Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta and an expanding universe of AI companies. The AI boom itself has become a central engine of the US stock-market growth. Nvidia's extraordinary appreciation, the enormous capital expenditure by hyperscalers, and the enthusiasm surrounding generative AI have helped drive technology valuations and major US indices. Nvidia had gained more than 1,700 per cent over the past four years before the recent reversal.Nvidia stock fell almost 10 per cent following Huang’s resignation before recovering, even as the broader market weathered the storm -- for now.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Home sales in the US are at their lowest level since 2016
articles.summary: The sale of previously owned homes dropped 5.5 percent in October, the lowest level since August 2010.
articles.body:
Sales of previously owned homes in the US have hit the lowest level since 2010 as mortgage rates hover above 7 percent.

The National Association of Realtors (NAR) said on Thursday that home sales dropped 5.5 percent in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million units. That was the lowest level since August 2010.

“Home buying is difficult when mortgage rates have climbed to their highest levels since 2000, aside from a single month in 2023. As a result, home sales fell to their lowest level since August 2010,” said NAR Chief Economist Lawrence Yun.

He said, “It is just a tough market for buyers and sellers.”

“Sales decreased by 8.8 percent year-over-year,” the NAR report found. “Month-over-month sales declined in the Midwest, South and West and held steady in the Northeast. Year-over-year sales declined in all four regions.”

The home sales used in the report are counted at the closing of a contract and are a look at previously occupied ones. October’s sales likely reflected contracts signed in August and September.

“Despite fewer transactions in October, the 88 million homeowners across the country are largely in a comfortable financial position due to sizable housing wealth accumulation,” said the report.

First-time buyers accounted for just 29 percent of home purchases last month, down from 31 percent in September and 32 percent in October last year, NAR said. First-time buyers have historically made up closer to 40 percent of home sales.

The US housing market has been in a slump since 2022, when mortgage rates increased from pandemic-era lows. Sales of previously occupied US homes were essentially flat last year, stuck at a 30-year low. Yun expects home sales this year will likely end up lower than in 2025.

The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 7.33 percent in October, according to the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation, more commonly known as Freddie Mac, up from 6.86 percent in September and 6.25 percent one year ago.

The rate, however, averaged 7.18 percent last week, down from 7.24 percent in the previous week.

Rates on home loans are influenced by inflation, Federal Reserve policy and bond-market investors’ expectations for the economy, among other factors. They generally follow the trajectory of the 10-year Treasury yield, which lenders use as a guide to pricing home loans.

Until the past few weeks, mortgage rates had been on the rise since late February, when the US war with Iran began, pushing up the price of oil and driving inflation higher. The run-up in rates also reflected heightened bond market volatility, which led to rising yields on US Treasuries.

articles.title: Turns out the AI king wasn’t untouchable
articles.summary: Big Tech CEOs have an aura of invincibility.
articles.body: Big Tech CEOs have an aura of invincibility. A small handful of men have amassed extraordinary power and run a collection of the world’s most valuable tech companies that make cutting-edge products fueling global markets and the economy. They’ve seldom been tested and never brought down. OpenAI tried and failed to fire its CEO Sam Altman. Elon Musk hung on to power after badly damaging Tesla’s reputation during his stint in politics. That invincibility myth was shattered Thursday when Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s CEO for 33 years, ally of the President of the United States and cofounder of the world’s most valuable AI company, resigned. Many business leaders have been taken down by scandals like Huang’s – the downfall of former CEOs of American Apparel, Boeing, Cisco, McDonald’s and Hewlett-Packard all played out in somewhat similar fashion. But none come close to the magnitude and significance of Huang’s ouster. “This is one of a kind,” said Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at the Yale School of Management. “In the corporate world, this is by far the biggest fall.” It sends a clear message: If Huang can be forced out, any leader can. It took a public scandal Huang appeared untouchable. He very well may have been – up until this week, before his infidelity spilled out into public view and could no longer be ignored by the board. Nvidia and Huang had been synonymous for decades. He maintained an extraordinarily flat organization, with 60 direct reports and no clear succession plan. He boasted that the company was structured such that he was uniquely qualified to run it. Huang’s genius was the stuff of legend. He correctly predicted in 2013 – a decade before ChatGPT – that the company’s graphics processors would serve as the foundation for AI. He was right, and his company became the first ever to be worth $5 trillion on the stock market. So the board failed to challenge Huang, despite numerous missteps and bad bets along the way. It was apparently unfazed by reports dating back more than a year about Nvidia’s odd relationship with Megaspeed – the major Nvidia customer run by Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese agent with whom Jensen Huang had a relationship. The board failed to investigate Huang when the New York Times reported last month that US intelligence feared Alice Huang may be a spy, or when photos of its CEO and Alice Huang were plastered all over the internet. It took the scandal becoming an unavoidable topic of public conversation this week for the board to hire an outside counsel to investigate. It took another revelation – by The New York Times that Huang had an alleged affair with an executive who reports to him – to ultimately force him to resign. That made the board negligent in its duties, said Nell Minow, chair of corporate governance advisory firm ValueEdge Advisors. “The single biggest failure of corporate boards is succession planning, and there’s no evidence that was done here,” said Minow. “We love to think about superstar CEOs and founders, but they’re never as special as they think they are.” Huang’s aura of invincibility stems from one of his favorite boasts: Nvidia’s humble 1993 founding during a meeting held at a Denny’s – and how its shaky beginnings forced him to repeatedly save the company from near extinction. He made the company’s motto: “Our company is 30 days from going out of business.” But the board misjudged that past success as evidence of Huang’s unique talents, Minow said. The biggest risk for the life of a company, she argued, is not failure – because when a company is on the verge of destruction, everyone is working together and problem solving. Instead, the biggest risk is when the company is doing spectacularly well: No one can sustain that hockey stick-like growth, and the board starts attributing success to intangible things like its uniquely talented leaders. “That puts a lot of pressure on the snowflake genius from Denny’s,” Minow said. “It’s like a baseball team with a winning streak no one can explain. The whole team starts wearing lucky socks. Nvidia’s board thought it had its lucky CEO.” The myth of the invincible tech CEO Huang may have wielded incredible power at Nvidia, but more recent tech founders have worked to place a buffer around themselves even more durable than Huang’s. Huang is an outlier among his tech CEO peers: He controls just 3.6% of his company’s shares. Many founders, including Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and soon-to-be public Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei all have dual class stock arrangements that give them significantly more voting power over common shareholders – and effectively unilateral power over their corporations’ governance. Even those stronger insulators are permeable. Shareholders aren’t powerless against dual class stock structures or seemingly untouchable CEOs: They can bombard companies with lawsuits – which have already started against Nvidia. And it’s not clear that even a CEO as wealthy and powerful as Musk could survive a scandal like Huang’s. Musk’s friendly, hand-picked Tesla board began a CEO replacement search and successfully pressured him to return his focus to the company after spending much of 2024 and 2025 engaged almost exclusively in the political spotlight, damaging Tesla’s global brand in the process. “There’s a lot of myth-making in tech that there’s one person who is uniquely qualified to run the company,” said Sonnenfeld. “That’s not true: They have human frailties, they’re imperfect, and they’re replaceable.” Nvidia board’s decision here was cut and dry: Anyone else at Nvidia would have been let go if they had engaged in Huang’s alleged conduct. Huang may have put his company’s trade secrets at risk of theft by a foreign competitor. He lost trust with Nvidia’s customers and demonstrated a lack of candor with his board. Huang lost the legitimacy to lead. So that means the CEO – even the visionary leader of the chipmaking bedrock of AI – can be held responsible, just like any other employee who may have violated the company’s code of conduct. And, on Thursday, he was kicked out of the company he built.

articles.title: Duolingo CEO on owl's guilt-trip reminders: 'Passive-aggressive works'
articles.summary: Duolingo's owl is still a winning strategy, keeping users motivated and using the app daily.
articles.body:
Sometimes the face of a company is a CEO in a leather jacket. Sometimes it's a giant green owl with a grudge.

At Yahoo Finance Invest , Duolingo ( DUOL ) co-founder and CEO Luis von Ahn said he never expected the language learning app's mascot, Duo the owl, to become so popular.

For several years, the owl has been memed online. Duo recently crashed Apple's ( AAPL ) foldable iPhone Duo launch, giving away free apples. But more often, he can be found guilt-tripping you with phone notifications.

"Some of our notifications … are passive-aggressive because we have found that passive-aggressive works," von Ahn told Yahoo Finance on Thursday. "You know, parents all over the place have found this too."

Business Insider once called Duolingo "the world's meanest app," but in 2026, Duolingo pledged to dial back the "unhinged" marketing — if only slightly.

"The owl is beloved all over the world," von Ahn said. "I think that's one of the reasons why people keep coming back to Duolingo."

Von Ahn told Yahoo Finance the company has also been able to cut back on costly AI spending mainly by switching from frontier models to open-weight models, reducing the cost of its AI video-call feature from about $0.30 per call to less than $0.01.

He added that Duolingo is shifting much of its other AI use, such as generating learning content, stories, and cartoons, to open-weight models as well.

"We're very happy with the cost reduction," von Ahn said. "We don't think we lost any kind of quality here. … The open-weight models are excellent."

articles.title: SpaceX and Tesla Talks on Record Merger Are Said to Progress
articles.summary: SpaceX and Tesla Inc. are progressing in their merger negotiations, setting the stage for a combination that could redefine the limits of global dealmaking.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- SpaceX and Tesla Inc. are progressing in their merger negotiations, setting the stage for a combination that could redefine the limits of global dealmaking.

Elon Musk's two largest companies could announce what would be the biggest-ever deal as soon as in December, according to people familiar with the matter. That aggressive timeline reflects Musk's tendency to move quickly when it comes to corporate maneuvers.

The companies have also discussed a scenario in which an announcement slips into early 2027, said the people, who asked to not be identified because the discussions are private. Their boards and advisers are hammering out the terms of the tie-up and governance structure of the combined entity, among other matters, the people said.

Representatives for Tesla and SpaceX didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

Tesla shares jumped to a session high, rising as much as 1.9%, while SpaceX stock gained 0.5% as of 3:20 p.m. Thursday in New York.

The merger would be a blockbuster for Wall Street's dealmakers, creating a conglomerate housing electric vehicles, energy storage batteries, rockets and satellites. The rationale for bringing all those assets under one roof lies in a shared ambition to leverage artificial intelligence across space, driverless cars and humanoid robots.

But both companies will have to grapple with obstacles before they can close a transaction, including how to ring-fence Tesla's operations in China, according to the people.

National security sensitivities around SpaceX's US government and defense contracts, and Tesla's large, profitable China manufacturing footprint, loom as "key dynamics that are at odds with each other" when it comes to getting regulatory and shareholder approvals for a deal, JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta told clients in a research note last month.

The merger would be a major test case for political sentiment following the US midterm elections. Democrats, which took control of Congress, have pledged to probe Musk's business and political dealings.

Musk in October said the boards of the companies had formed special committees of independent board directors to consider combining.

articles.title: Nvidia executive Ian Buck emerges as CEO frontrunner on prediction markets
articles.summary: Prediction markets are pointing to Nvidia VP Ian Buck as a frontrunner for permanent CEO role.
articles.body:
With Jensen Huang out as CEO at Nvidia ( NVDA ) and CFO Colette Kress taking on the role of interim CEO, Wall Street, the company's partners, and its customers are waiting to find out who the next permanent CEO will be.

There are a number of candidates inside and outside of the company who could fill the position. But prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket have zeroed in on Nvidia VP of hyperscale and high-performance computing Ian Buck as the company's next leader.

Both sites rank the odds of Buck taking over at roughly 40%.

Buck has worked at Nvidia for the last 22 years, rising from a systems engineer to his current role as the head of the company's biggest businesses.

The executive also has the kind of engineering chops that Nvidia's board may find compelling for the CEO role.

Buck has a Ph.D. from Stanford University in computer science and, more importantly, developed Nvidia's CUDA technology.

CUDA allows companies to use the chip giant's graphics processing units (GPUs) for general computing, a capability that was instrumental in turning Nvidia into the AI powerhouse it is today.

But Buck has a hard act to follow. Huang's charismatic personality drew customers and investors, turning him into one of the tech industry's biggest stars.

And his penchant for elaborate keynotes at massive venues, where he regularly offered technical deep dives, drew thousands of attendees. It's unclear if any other executive could check all of the same boxes.

For now, Wall Street analysts see Kress as a steady hand to guide Nvidia through the current storm.

KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst John Vinh wrote in a note to investors that Kress's appointment as interim CEO is constructive "given her tenure as CFO since 2013 and deep institutional knowledge of Nvidia's business and strategy."

Whoever Nvidia's board eventually chooses to lead the company will have plenty of questions to answer about its future and whether it can continue to dominate the industry as it did under Huang.

articles.title: Stock market has a 'worrisome' focus on Anthropic IPO, Ariel Investments' Mellody Hobson says
articles.summary: The markets are looking overvalued, warned one of the best value-seekers in finance.
articles.body:
Markets are looking a bit disturbing, according to corporate America powerhouse Mellody Hobson.

"It's worrisome when you start to read articles that say the whole market will go the way of one IPO, specifically Anthropic," Hobson, the co-CEO of Ariel Investments, said at the end of October when asked about her assessment of the markets at the moment.

"That feels a little single-minded … when you consider a market of thousands of stocks of different industries and the like. So, it shows how many chips are in the middle of the table on this one trade. And we are not traders; we're investors at Ariel. So it goes against all of our natural inclinations."

Hobson has established herself as one of the most influential figures in corporate finance, rising from a summer intern to co-CEO and president of value-oriented Ariel Investments alongside founder John Rogers.

She is the former chair of coffee giant Starbucks ( SBUX ), continues to serve on the board of JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ), and is a minority owner in the NFL's Denver Broncos.

Her decades of investing experience — rooted in finding out-of-favor stocks with big upside potential — are being put to the test right now.

Market volatility has spiked in recent weeks due to the midterm elections ; high-stakes Big Tech earnings prints, with mixed reports and heavy capital expenditure outlays; and the removal of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, triggering a sharp sell-off in hot sectors.

At the same time, macro headwinds have intensified as crude oil prices remain elevated amid geopolitical friction in the Middle East, reigniting fears of sticky headline inflation and keeping long-duration Treasury yields pinned near multiyear highs.

"It feels very 1999, you know, partying like we're in 1999 again, where it was that same dot-com conversation," Hobson explained. "I think the reason that it's gotten frothy from our perspective is you have a lot of people chasing the same things. You also have this willingness to have this level of investment with no clear understanding of the payoff."

"We've seen fits and starts on that," Hobson continued. "So there are times the market says it's going to work out again; that feels a little dot-com. And then there are other times that the market says, well, wait a minute, we're spending billions and billions, trillions of dollars, but we don't know what it means in profits. articles.title: Bill Ackman calls Anthropic 'the most amazing business story of this century' — but he's not a buyer
articles.summary: Famed investor Bill Ackman takes a somewhat cautious view on Anthropic.
articles.body:
Pershing Square Capital CEO Bill Ackman thinks Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) is a great story with a business that has real potential. Just don't expect him to be a buyer early on when Anthropic becomes publicly traded.

"We think of ourselves as very low-risk investors. We want to invest in businesses that we can predict with a very high degree of confidence," the well-known value investor said at Yahoo Finance Invest. "I think Anthropic is perhaps the most amazing business story of this century in terms of from zero to where it is today — it's an absolutely remarkable story. An incredibly impressive story. I think it's just a much more complicated question as to what that business is worth. It's very hard to nail that with any degree of precision. It could be worth a lot more, a lot less, depending upon a few variables that are difficult to predict. And that's why it doesn't fit into our portfolio."

Anthropic has set an IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share, targeting a fully diluted valuation of approximately $1.4 trillion. The company could raise up to $100 billion from its IPO at the high end of the range.

But the business has a lot to prove to justify keeping such a lofty valuation in public markets.

articles.title: Why Vanguard CEO Salim Ramji sees a 'disturbing' trend with prediction markets
articles.summary: Prediction markets have created a new risk factor in the investing world, Vanguard CEO Salim Ramji says.
articles.body:
Vanguard was founded on the principle of staying patient in investing, with both eyes always focused on the long-term.

The rise of prediction markets is creating a wildly different dynamic, especially with younger investors, Vanguard CEO Salim Ramji said.

"The good news is, for a 25-year-old investor today, one out of three of them have an investment account. That's six times more than was the case 10 years ago. And that's a really good thing," Ramji said at Yahoo Finance Invest.

"The challenge, to my mind, is that there's another one-third of 25-year-olds who are outside of the traditional investments system. They're looking at online betting platforms. They're looking at things like prediction markets or crypto or sports betting. And if someone's just doing that, you know, for their fun money on the side, fine," he said.

Ramji cautioned, however, "The really disturbing thing is that when we survey those clients, 80% of them are doing those activities because they think it's a fast track to financial success. And the biggest problem I see in the investment landscape today is that people are blurring the lines between investing and gambling."

Vanguard is a global financial powerhouse founded in 1975 by the legendary Jack Bogle, who died in 2019 at age 89 and became known as the "father of simple investing." He revolutionized retail investing by championing ultra-low-cost index investing.

He also pounded home the message in TV appearances about the benefits of portfolio diversification and patience in growing one's wealth.

Today, the asset management behemoth serves tens of millions of individual investors worldwide and oversees approximately $12 trillion in assets under management.

Ramji has headed up Vanguard since July 2024. He is a former senior partner at McKinsey & Company and longtime corporate lawyer — and the first external hire ever selected to lead Vanguard since its inception.

He spent a decade at archrival BlackRock ( BLK ) as global head of iShares and index investments, where he directed the massive worldwide expansion of exchange-traded funds and managed trillions in passive capital.

Since assuming leadership, Ramji has focused on modernizing Vanguard's technological infrastructure and integrating generative AI client tools.

articles.title: United Airlines CEO is still open to buying rival American Airlines. He just needs a 'willing partner.'
articles.summary: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby still wants to make a deal, possibly a big one.
articles.body:
United Airlines ( UAL ) CEO Scott Kirby remains a big believer that the next wave of consolidation in the airline industry has to happen as it seeks to grow profits amid higher fuel bills and rising costs to premiumize planes.

He still thinks United is poised to do the consolidating, provided he isn't rebuffed, as he was earlier this year by his former employer American Airlines ( AAL ).

"I think the biggest impediment is having a willing partner," Kirby said at Yahoo Finance Invest on whether he would make another play to merge with American Airlines. "I am more convinced today than I was when I wrote my note six months ago that it could get approval. It could get approval because it is good for customers. So many people look at that kind of a merger through what has been the traditional airline commodity lens, that air travel is a commodity, and it doesn't matter which airline flies. But customers care about the service, the product, the technology, the reliability."

"It wouldn't be easy," Kirby acknowledged. "We'd have to do some divestitures, but I 100% think it could get approved."

In April, Kirby shocked the airline industry by making an audacious overture to merge with American Airlines.

Kirby pitched the ambitious combination as a historic play to build an undisputed global champion capable of restoring American leadership against foreign flag carriers and dramatically expanding network scale.

The proposed tie-up immediately sparked fierce antitrust pushback in Washington.

The overture unraveled within days when American Airlines CEO Robert Isom abruptly shuttered the proposal, issuing a public statement declaring that American was not engaged in nor interested in any merger discussions. Kirby later revealed he was blindsided by American's public rejection via press release.

No doubt a merger of this kind would have considerable roadblocks to clear, from antitrust concerns to the inevitable concerns of labor unions.

But something may have to happen, and possibly in 2027 if fuel prices stay high and continue to hammer profits, experts say.

"We believe in the merits of industry consolidation, chiefly because it theoretically results in more prudent deployment of capital, leading to higher returns," JPMorgan analyst Mark Streeter said. "We also believe consolidation leads to hub rationalization and the elimination of duplicative costs. We also wrote over 20 years ago that deals beget more deals. More recently, as the merits of loyalty became increasingly clear, we emphasized the importance of national scale when it comes to credit card economics."

articles.title: Lawmakers react as Huang leaves Nvidia

articles.body:
Lawmakers on Capitol Hill reacted Thursday to the news of Jensen Huang resigning as Nvidia CEO, a move that ushers in a new era at one of the world’s most powerful companies.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) said Huang’s departure was up the Nvidia board of directors, adding it was “not unexpected.”

Outgoing Rep. Marc Veasey (D-Texas) noted Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy “should be a wake up call” for Americans, telling me Beijing was “trying to gain access to a company that works on important AI” issues.

Veasey also noted the impact of Huang’s departure on the stock market. Shares of Nvidia dipped below $150 per on Thursday for the first time since June 2025, closing at $166.19.

The three major stock indices also took slight hits, falling by less than 0.4 percent relative to Wednesday’s closing bell.

Sen. Jim Justice (R-W.V.) referenced the “amazing” impact Nvidia has on the economy, and said Huang’s departure could affect the broader economy.

“The magnitude of that impact, I can’t tell you,” Justice told The Hill.

My colleagues Mike Lillis , Miranda Nazzaro and Julia Shapero have a story out on lawmakers wanting answers from Huang, Nvidia and the Trump administration about the ordeal .

articles.title: Bill Ackman says Microsoft's position is 'really, really strong' as Anthropic pushes into enterprise software
articles.summary: Bill Ackman makes the case for buying the dip on Microsoft.
articles.body:
Billionaire investor Bill Ackman remains bullish on Microsoft ( MSFT ) despite Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) becoming more aggressive in the enterprise software tools front.

"We think they're doing a very good job staying current in terms of enabling a new AI generation of workers," the famed value investor and CEO of Pershing Square Capital Management said at Yahoo Finance Invest.

"We think Microsoft's position is really, really strong," Ackman added. "I think Microsoft's position really remains a powerful one."

Ackman began buying Microsoft earlier this year, and has said he views it as a core holding.

Anthropic, meanwhile, just sent a message to the software space led by Microsoft and its Office suite. The AI company targeted a large piece of Microsoft's business in part to justify its exorbitant valuation.

Soaring fuel prices will lead to 'a reckoning' for airlines: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby

United Airlines CEO is still open to buying rival American Airlines. He just needs a 'willing partner.'

Vanguard CEO Salim Ramji warns bond market volatility could be a key 2027 risk

Coinciding with its roadshow launch, Anthropic released several new features late Tuesday, including Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets in beta. It also pushed Claude Dashboards to general availability as Claude Data.

The tools are available on all paid plans and extend Anthropic's efforts to bring more functionality directly within Claude.

The unveiling sent Microsoft shares lower amid fears of a true new rival to the tech giant's Office franchise. Shares are down 2.4% over the past five days.

"There is no question given Anthropic's unprecedented growth, deep technical expertise and substantial financial resources this new product offering bears watching," Stifel analyst Brad Reback wrote to clients. "That said, we do NOT expect these products to have any meaningful impact on M365 growth rates for the foreseeable future based on deep enterprise integration, security/governance and MSFT's complete commitment to ensuring customer IP sovereignty."

articles.title: Nvidia market cap plunges $490 billion following former CEO Huang's affair scandals
articles.summary: Nvidia's market cap has plummeted nearly half a trillion dollars.
articles.body:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) has shed a whopping $490 billion in market value after former CEO Jensen Huang's affair scandals shocked the tech world and beyond.

The company closed out the trading week last Friday with a market cap of $4.498 trillion. That plunged to $4.005 trillion at the end of trading Thursday. Apple's market cap stands at $5.16 trillion.

Nvidia was valued at as much as $5.75 trillion as recently as Oct. 5. But a rout in the AI trade and Huang's reported affairs have sent the company's valuation plummeting by roughly $1.75 trillion.

This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

Huang initially admitted to having an affair on Sunday . Though he didn't name the person, reports allege it was Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy.

On Wednesday, The New York Times reported that Huang had a second affair with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell .

Huang resigned as CEO Thursday morning , and the company's board replaced him with CFO Colette Kress , who will serve as interim CEO.

Reuters has since reported that Huang was allegedly involved in a relationship with a second employee.

articles.title: RBI may hike rates by up to 50 bps in FY27: Economists
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Economists expect the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to raise key policy rates after the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting in early Dec to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Economists expect the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to raise key policy rates after the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting in early Dec to check rising inflation. Following its first policy rate hike in over three years in Oct, they expect the MPC to raise the repo rate by another 25-50 basis points during the current financial year (100 basis points equal a percentage point).An increase in repo rates, the rate at which banks borrow from RBI overnight, will translate into a rise in EMIs on home and other loans, while helping depositors earn more.Dipti Deshpande, principal economist of Crisil Ratings said inflation is expected to average 5.3% in 2026-27, with risks tilted on the upside as food inflation continues to surprise on the upside. "The implications for MPC are clear and (I) expect RBI to retain its tightening bias and see scope for another 25bps hike in Dec review meeting," she said.SBI said the odds have decisively shifted towards a 25-basis points (bps) rate hike in Dec instead of 50 bps projected earlier, driven by four key factors: A more stable rupee, revival in capital flows, softer oil price outlook and easing US Treasury yields. "Importantly, expectations of three-to-four successive rate hikes, which had gained traction earlier, now appear to be an outlier. We expect the Dec hike to be followed by a more data-dependent policy approach."CareEdge Ratings economist Rajani Sinha also expects a 25bps rate hike in Dec. Echoing similar views, ICRA chief economist Aditi Nayar said with the CPI inflation set to remain above 6% and GDP growth likely to ease only slightly in Q2, a further 25 bps rate hike in Dec appears almost certain. "Thereafter, the trajectory of crude oil prices, which have cooled in the recent sessions, will be critical in shaping the need for and extent of additional rate tightening in 2027," she said."(RBI's) Oct policy stance indicates its preference for addressing emerging inflationary pressures and anchoring inflation expectations, with a scope of 25bps hike in Dec," said Vivek Rathi, national director, Knight Frank India.Kotak Mahindra Bank chief economist Upasna Bhardwaj, however, said with inflation expected to remain elevated above 6%, amid adverse base effect from GST, higher food prices and partial pass through of higher commodity prices, RBI is expected to hike rates by 50 bps in 2026-27, with further upside risks likely if food inflation flares up significantly or benign oil prices reverse trajectory.Elara Capital economist Garima Kapoor expects an increase of another 50 bps over next six-to-nine months as inflation is unlikely to cool off immediately, as pass through of previous hikes continues. HDFC Bank principal economist Sakshi Gupta also expects a cumulative 50 bps hike in coming months, with RBI expected to deliver a 25 bps rate hike at both its Dec and Feb meetings.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Smartphone sales fall 20% by volume
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Offline smartphone sales fell 18-20% by volume during the Diwali season, according to the All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA), even
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Offline smartphone sales fell 18-20% by volume during the Diwali season, according to the All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA), even as sales value stayed flat. The slowdown was visible earlier throughout the festive season. Counterpoint Research estimated that smartphone sales volumes fell 20% year-on-year across the first two waves of festive sales through late Oct, covering Navratri and Dussehra.Days after Diwali, two Indian smartphone brands are raising prices by up to Rs 3,000. Ai+ Smartphone has already pushed two models past the Rs 10,000 mark, while Lava will raise prices from Nov 15. Both companies cited higher memory costs.The hikes come as the entry-level market is shrinking sharply. Shipments of smartphones priced below Rs 10,000 fell 65% year-on-year in the first half of 2026, according to Counterpoint. The segment accounted for just 4% of overall shipments in April-June, down from 18% in July-Sept 2025. The pressure extended to costlier phones in the Sept quarter, when shipments below Rs 20,000 fell 47% year-on-year, compared with a 20% decline for the overall market.Ai+ raised prices by Rs 1,000 to Rs 3,000 on select variants on Nov 11. The 4GB RAM and 64GB storage versions of its Pulse 2 and Pulse 2 FE went from Rs 8,999 to Rs 10,999, an increase of about 22%. The company brought forward the hike by four days, citing higher memory and other component costs for fresh stock.Lava said ongoing memory shortages had prompted a price increase of up to Rs 3,000 across its smartphone portfolio from Nov 15. It said festive prices would remain available online and in stores until the revision takes effect.Counterpoint said rising DRAM and NAND memory costs had already triggered several rounds of handset price hikes, leaving brands less room for deep festive discounts. Higher prices have led some shoppers to delay upgrades and made financing and trade-in offers more important for those still looking to buy.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: OpenAI lets biz to get AI requests processed in India
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: OpenAI on Thursday said eligible businesses can now have some of their AI requests processed on servers in India.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: OpenAI on Thursday said eligible businesses can now have some of their AI requests processed on servers in India. The option could help banks, payments firms and other companies that need to keep certain data within the country when using AI. OpenAI already offered eligible customers the option to store data in India. The change is that the model can now process supported requests here too. If a company asks the model to summarise an internal document, for instance, the computing needed to read the document and generate the summary can take place in India.The service initially covers OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna model and is available to businesses and developers that use the company's API to build AI into their own software. To use it, customers need to set up a new project and select India as the location for both data storage and processing. The rollout is limited to direct API customers.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Microsoft outage strands office workers nationwide
articles.summary: Microsoft’s widespread outage left users across the United States unable to access their Outlook email, leaving office workers stranded (or celebrating).
articles.body: Microsoft’s widespread outage left users across the United States unable to access their Outlook email, leaving office workers stranded (or celebrating). “We’re investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas,” the company posted on X Thursday afternoon. While reports of Outlook outages have decreased from a peak of more than 130,000 earlier in the afternoon, as of 3:30 pm EST almost 60,000 users reported issues, according to Downdetector. The outage appears to have began shortly after noon. The outage continued for much of the 9-5 workday across the United States; the company later said it is “aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact.” Earlier in the day, it said in an update that the problems stem from “failed health checks may originate from a specific component on the affected servers that’s responsible for processing them.” Later on, it said it was restarting those servers because they “have become unresponsive.” Microsoft said the potentially impacted services include: Meanwhile, many in Corporate America don’t seem to be in much of a rush. “no outlook, no teams…. how about we all just go home,” one X user posted today.
